content:
devon: FYI: apac1 dedicated racks showing spike in tail latency for a small set of tenants. not GPU CPU related  high retransmits on egress and packet send errors.
emma: can you paste one of the host logs?
devon: grep output and tcpdump snippet: 
```
Aug 12 15:40:02 kernel: IP x.x.x.x > y.y.y.y: Fragmentation needed and DF set (mtu=1500)
15:40:02.998 tcpdump: IPIP: GREv1, proto 4, length 1280
```
matt: classic PMTU blackhole. looks like some racks have mtu 9000, overlay path drops to 1500. SR-IOV VF vs overlay mismatch.
lina: last week we updated edge-proxy kernels to stricter DF handling, so earlier tolerant hosts now fail. some tenants stream large gRPC frames (runtime->proxy) so retransmits blow p99.
sophia: is shared pool affected? or only dedicated slices pinned to those racks?
devon: primarily dedicated slices pinned by NIC profile. shared takes a different egress path that includes MSS clamp.
aj: quick stopgap?
matt: two immediate options: 1) apply MSS clamping at LB (needs net ticket + rolling LB restarts) or 2) enable net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing via daemonset on affected nodes to recover via probing.
emma: note: probing only heals new connections. we have long-lived streams (kv cache, websockets), so expect partial improvement.
devon: propose playbook:
- emergency (5-15m): daemonset to set net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=2 across apac1 hosts (canary 20% then full)
- short (tonight): add iptables MSS clamp on edge-proxy LBs (NET-412) and roll proxies off-peak
- medium (hours): temporary egress carveout for hottest tenants route via egress-vlan-2 (MSS clamp path). estimated cross-az transit cost ~ $300/day per tenant carveout for high-throughput tenants
- long: unify MTU across rack/overlay and add PMTU symptom alerting to console + runbook

sophia: +1. who owns the daemonset and the LB change?
aj: I can push the daemonset. Will prepare a tiny init script that sets sysctl and restarts stream consumers.
matt: I'll open NET-412 to add MSS clamp at LB and coordinate off-peak restarts.
lina: devon, list affected tenants and their slices so product can evaluate carveout costs.
devon: affected IDs: t-14001, t-14002, t-14099. t-14002 accounts for ~70% of retransmit volume.
infra-bot: alert: apac1-edge-proxy-02 reported if_in_errors spike 2025-08-12T15:43:10Z :exclamation: 
aj: canary daemonset ready. applying to 20% apac1 in 1m.
sophia: monitoring ask: add an alert rule for "Fragmentation needed and DF set" > 5/min per node and p99 token latency > 200ms for dedicated pools.
emma: also instrument TLS/frame sizes from runtime to see which clients send > 1200B frames that hit DF.
devon: agreed. if daemonset doesn't drop p99 within 10m we proceed with carveout for t-14002. product ok with temporary carveout budget up to $800/day.
matt: NET-412 opened: plan to add MSS clamp on LB and schedule rolling proxy restart at 23:00 local. link: https://net.company/NET-412
aj: sysctl to set: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=2` and persist by writing `/etc/sysctl.d/99-pmtu.conf`. restart policy in daemonset will SIGHUP stream processes.
emma: note for runbook: before scaling pools check node dmesg for "Fragmentation needed and DF set" and run `ss -s` to inspect retransmits.
infra-bot: deploy: mtu-probe-daemonset canary applied to apac1 (pods: 4/4) 2025-08-12T15:48:26Z :white_check_mark: 
aj: canary metrics: observed p99 drop from 510ms -> 140ms on canary hosts. retransmits down ~65%. rolling remaining nodes now.
lina: nice. track carveout cost and ops-summary if we flip carveout.
devon: updating incident doc with tenant list + owners. will add followup tasks for MTU harmonization and PMTU monitoring. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
